sourceObjective: Past routines with the imperfect: Use the imperfect for past habits or background: estudiaba, comía, vivía.
sourceSpeaking: Role-play Antes y ahora with a patient classmate. Practice past routines with the imperfect. Use this lesson's grammar, ask a related question, answer the partner, and confirm understanding. Keep language at beginner level; explain unfamiliar words in English when asked.

cards.candidateNote: La can be an article or an object pronoun depending on context.
Une is used with feminine nouns, as in une autre ville. Sac à dos is masculine and takes un.
Sac is masculine, so use un sac à dos.
Dans means inside (dans une autre ville); sur means on top of; à can mark a place or destination (à la bibliothèque). These are separate words.
Bleu agrees with a masculine noun; bleue with a feminine noun.
Les is a plural article or object pronoun, regardless of gender.

cards.sourceSpanish: Antes vivía cerca de la escuela.
cards.sourceEnglish: I used to live near the school.
I used to study Spanish in the afternoon.
cards.candidateNote: Language names take an article after étudier: étudier l’espagnol.

cards.sourceEnglish: Ana used to walk to the library.
cards.candidateFrench: Ana allait à pied à la bibliothèque.

cards.sourceEnglish: We used to eat together on Fridays.
cards.candidateNote: Le vendredi means every Friday, a repeated habit.

cards.candidateFrench: Luis avait un sac à dos bleu.

cards.sourceEnglish: Now we live in another city.
cards.candidateFrench: Maintenant, nous habitons dans une autre ville.

disputedFaces.question: The slashes do not pair positionally. English temporal in/on in Readers2/4 is expressed by French articles l’après-midi/le vendredi; destination à in Reader3 renders to; Reader6 dans renders in. Sur is unattested in this Reader. Grouped scoring needs context.
French bleu/bleue is selected by noun gender. Reader5 attests masculine bleu with sac à dos; feminine bleue is not in these Reader turns.
Spanish los is masculine plural, matching the pinned English qualifier. French les covers both genders and cannot be taught as masculine-only. A source-vs-French note must be visible.

speakingCandidate: Role-play Avant et maintenant with a patient classmate. Use the imparfait to say where you used to live, what you used to study in the afternoon, how Ana got to the library, when you ate together, and what backpack Luis had. Then say where you live now. Ask a related question, answer your partner, and confirm understanding. Keep to beginner French; explain unfamiliar words in English when asked.
sourceQuestions: Spanish los is masculine plural, but French les is gender neutral; a paired card cannot carry the Spanish qualifier as a French restriction.
The slash-separated dans / sur / à proposal cannot be scored positionally against in / on / at. The Reader attests temporal French articles, à for destination, and dans for location; sur is absent.
Bleu / bleue depends on noun gender. Reader 5 attests masculine bleu with sac à dos, not feminine bleue.
